nativeValidation.setup: Use a clean disposable checkout at this commit on each test host or native guest. Run the first two commands from the repository root, copy the probe to files.copyTo, then run the remaining commands in order. Run macOS as an unprivileged user. Run Windows in Windows PowerShell 5.1 with its normal current-user profile. Save console output for each platform.

windows: if ((git rev-parse HEAD).Trim() -ne 'b07e1ea8425fe29739eb35cde9c266e10ec4e2b3') { throw 'Unexpected worker revision' }
go build -buildvcs=true -overlay=.t3-tmp/native/overlay.json -o .t3-tmp/native/probe.exe ./servers/sandrun-api/cmd/credential-cleanup-probe; if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Probe build failed' }
go build -buildvcs=true -o .t3-tmp/native/ownsand-guest.exe ./cmds/ownsand-guest; if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Guest helper build failed' }
macos: export CGO_ENABLED=0 TMPDIR="$PWD/.t3-tmp/native"; go env GOOS GOARCH

expectedResults: Go reports the native host OS and architecture. Both binaries report the worker SHA and vcs.modified=false.

The probe starts the actual OwnSand GuestService on a disposable loopback listener. Windows holds the credential open without delete sharing while permitting the read. macOS makes the credential directory unwritable.
Blocked scenario: exit=22, marker=false, credential-file=true, exec-output=0, runner-output=0 and credential-in-diagnostics=false.

Successful scenario: exit=0, marker=true, credential-file=false, exec-output=0, redirected=true and credential-in-diagnostics=false. The marker checks the credential in its environment and checks that the file is already gone at invocation.

The probe exits 0 and prints CREDENTIAL_CLEANUP_PROBE_PASS. The probe stops its guest helper and removes its fixture files. The SandRun sandbox teardown path was exercised separately on Linux with PostgreSQL and a fake OwnSand control plane.
